newsitem.title: USA: Narcotics fugitive Torres back in United States.
newsitem.headline: Narcotics fugitive Torres back in United States.

text.p: Suspected cocaine trafficker Oscar Alberto Torres, one of the United States' most wanted fugitives, has been brought back to the United States from Colombia, the U.S. Marshals Service said Thursday.

Torres, a 53-year-old Cuban national, was arrested in Baranquilla, Colombia, earlier this week. He was flown to Miami under escort Wednesday night and was due to appear in a Miami court for legal formalities.

Torres escaped from custody in Macon, Ga. in 1993, while he was awaiting trail and a possible life sentence for possession and intention to distribute 110 pounds (50 kg) of cocaine. With help from outside, he managed to cut through cell bars and security fences at the Moultrie County Jail.
"We considered Torres a dangerous fugitive and placed a high priority on his arrest," Marshals Service Director Eduardo Gonzalez said.
Torres has a criminal history dating back to 1962 and is believed to be involved with international drug smuggling networks, the marshals service said.
